headline_hook: Claude Code Ships Agent Orchestration While Surya OCR 2 Tops Models 5× Its Size
preview_topics: the UK opens its AI safety playbook

pick_of_the_day.thesis: OpenRouter's $113M raise confirms that the model layer is commoditizing faster than anyone expected — the real moat isn't making models, it's the routing intelligence that picks the right one for each task, and that reshapes how every builder should think about vendor lock-in.

model_literacy.relevance: Claude Code's dynamic workflows generate a deterministic script before execution rather than letting the agent improvise each step — today's news on workflows, Tool Search, and effort-level control all reflect the industry shifting from 'let the model figure it out' to structured orchestration with explicit control surfaces.

items.title: Surya OCR 2 Hits 83% on OlmOCR — Best Under 3B, 91 Languages
items.angle: Practical OCR that runs on modest hardware just leapfrogged models 5× its size — if you've been waiting for on-device document understanding, the math finally works.
items.key_fact: 83.3% on OlmOCR benchmark, top score for any model under 3B parameters

items.title: OpenAI Deploys Rosalind for Allied Government Biodefense
items.angle: AI moving from productivity tooling into national security infrastructure — this is what 'dual-use' looks like when governments are the customer.
items.key_fact: Expanding GPT-Rosalind access to allied government partners for pandemic preparedness

items.title: Opus 4.8: The Coding Model That Knows When to Stop
items.angle: Felix Rieseberg's firsthand take cuts through benchmarks — Opus 4.8's real edge is judgment about scope and steering, not raw performance.
items.key_fact: Strongest coding model with notably better judgment on task scope

items.title: Koji: The AI Tutor That Makes Kids Think Instead of Copy
items.angle: 10K+ likes signal this hit the nerve of every parent worried AI makes kids dumber — Koji's approach guides reasoning instead of dispensing answers.
items.key_fact: 10,938 likes, designed to build understanding rather than give answers

items.title: Inside Claude Code's Dynamic Workflows: Deterministic Scripts, Parallel Agents
items.angle: The engineering lead explains the architecture — Claude generates a deterministic orchestration script then fans out across parallel agents, not the chat-loop-picks-next-tool pattern everyone assumes.
items.key_fact: 9,701 likes; Claude writes the orchestration script, then executes it across parallel agents

items.title: Claude Code Auto Mode Lands on Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry
items.angle: Enterprise teams on non-direct API were locked out of Claude Code's most autonomous mode — that gate just opened for Opus 4.7/4.8.
items.key_fact: Auto mode now available on all three major cloud provider integrations

items.title: Codex Gets Persistent Visual Identicons for Background Agents
items.angle: A small UX detail that matters when you're juggling multiple concurrent agents — stable pixel identicons across tabs and transcripts.
items.key_fact: Stable identicons persist across tabs and transcripts

items.title: Claude Code Now Lets You Dial Effort Level Per Task
items.angle: The /effort command and Cowork integration give you a practical lever for the speed-vs-depth tradeoff — stop paying for deep thinking on trivial changes.
items.key_fact: Granular effort control via /effort command and Cowork mode

items.title: Hermes Agent Adds On-Demand Tool Schema Loading for MCP
items.angle: With 15+ MCP servers, tool schemas devour context before the agent does any work — loading on-demand is a pattern every MCP-heavy setup should steal.
items.key_fact: Tool Search loads MCP schemas on-demand instead of upfront context consumption

items.title: UK AI Safety Institute Open-Sources Its Evaluation Datasets
items.angle: Government-grade safety evals are now public and reproducible — anyone can now audit and build on the methodology the UK uses to test frontier models.
items.key_fact: Full evaluation datasets and methodology released publicly

items.title: Simon Willison Breaks Down How Anthropic Contains Claude Across Products
items.angle: Practical security architecture for multi-product LLM deployment — the containment patterns here apply to anyone shipping AI in more than one surface.
items.key_fact: Detailed analysis of Anthropic's cross-product containment architecture

items.title: OpenRouter Raises $113M to Be the Routing Layer for Multi-Model AI
items.angle: The model routing layer just raised a war chest — a $113M signal that multi-model is the default architecture, not a hedging strategy.
items.key_fact: $113M Series B for the platform routing across Claude, GPT, Gemini, and dozens more

items.title: Mollick: Organizations Are Underinvesting in AI Capacity-Building
items.angle: The split between 'build things with AI' and 'build capacity to build things with AI' — most orgs are all-in on the first and ignoring the second.
items.key_fact: Two categories of AI investment: building things vs. building capacity to build things

items.title: Is AI-Generated Code Recreating Frontend's Lost Decade?
items.angle: A sharp argument that AI code generation is producing jQuery-era complexity debt at 10× speed — worth reading whether you agree or not.
items.key_fact: Essay draws parallels between jQuery/Angular/React churn and AI-generated code complexity

items.title: webstandards.dev: A Source-Cited Spec for SEO, A11y, Security, and Agent-Readiness
items.angle: Joost de Valk's comprehensive reference where every claim cites a source — replace your team's ad-hoc checklist with this.
items.key_fact: Platform-agnostic spec covering SEO, accessibility, security, and AI agent readiness

items.title: OpenAI Voice Hack Night: 4 Realtime Voice Agents Built in 6 Hours
items.angle: The voice AI developer loop is now fast enough for hackathon-quality builds in a single evening — the gap between demo and product is shrinking.
items.key_fact: 4 production-quality realtime voice agent projects built in 6 hours

items.title: Gradio 'Build Small' Hackathon: Max 32B Params, Must Fit on a Laptop
items.angle: A refreshing constraint-driven hackathon — when you can't scale, you optimize. Sponsored by OpenAI, NVIDIA, and OpenBMB.
items.key_fact: Max 32B parameters, must fit on a laptop; sponsored by OpenAI, NVIDIA, OpenBMB
